## unknown-region-type

**Severity:** error · **Phase:** structure · **Applies to:** every region

`data-editable` must name a known region type, and `<editable-*>` elements must be known region elements.

The runtime replaces an element with an unknown `data-editable` type with an error card. An unknown `<editable-*>` element never hydrates, but still counts as the parent region for everything inside it.

**Mirrors:**

- editable-regions/helpers/hydrate-editable-regions.ts:15-22,87-103
- editable-regions/nodes/editable.ts:480-494

Fixtures: [src/rules/unknown-region-type](src/rules/unknown-region-type)

## text-requires-prop

**Severity:** error · **Phase:** structure · **Applies to:** `text`

Text regions need a `data-prop` attribute.

Without `data-prop` the runtime shows an error card instead of the text. An empty `data-prop=""` is valid and binds the parent's value, e.g. a plain-string array item.

**Mirrors:**

- editable-regions/nodes/editable-text.ts:20-29

Fixtures: [src/rules/text-requires-prop](src/rules/text-requires-prop)

## array-item-requires-array

**Severity:** error · **Phase:** structure · **Applies to:** `array-item`

Array items must be nested inside an array region, with no other region in between.

The runtime checks the nearest parent region. If it isn't an array, the item shows an error card and gets no controls. A common cause is double nesting: a component whose output starts with its own `array-item`, inside the `array-item` the page template already adds.

**Mirrors:**

- editable-regions/nodes/editable-array-item.ts:34-48

Fixtures: [src/rules/array-item-requires-array](src/rules/array-item-requires-array)

## array-requires-items

**Severity:** error · **Phase:** structure · **Applies to:** `array`

An array region needs at least one array item, a `<template>`, or a `data-component`/`data-component-key` attribute.

New items are built by copying an existing item, cloning a `<template>`, or rendering a registered component. With none of those, adding an item shows an error card.

**Mirrors:**

- editable-regions/nodes/editable-array.ts:270,290-316
- docs: visual-editing-reference.md § When HTML <template> blueprints are needed

Fixtures: [src/rules/array-requires-items](src/rules/array-requires-items)

## array-non-item-children

**Severity:** warn · **Phase:** structure · **Applies to:** `array`

Every direct child of an array region should be, or contain, one of its array items.

Static siblings inside an array (a logo, a "see all" link) are left behind or duplicated when items are added, removed or reordered. Split the layout container from the array container; `display: contents` on the array wrapper keeps grid and flex layouts intact.

**Mirrors:**

- docs: visual-editing-reference.md § Don't mix array items with non-array siblings

Fixtures: [src/rules/array-non-item-children](src/rules/array-non-item-children)

## array-keyed-item-missing-id

**Severity:** warn · **Phase:** structure · **Applies to:** `array`

When an array sets `data-id-key` or `data-component-key`, each item needs a `data-id` or `data-component`.

A keyed array matches items to its data by `data-id` (falling back to `data-component`). An item with neither never matches, so it's thrown away and rebuilt on every update, losing its live DOM.

**Mirrors:**

- editable-regions/nodes/editable-array.ts:270,338-375

Fixtures: [src/rules/array-keyed-item-missing-id](src/rules/array-keyed-item-missing-id)

## component-empty-prop

**Severity:** warn · **Phase:** structure · **Applies to:** `component`

Component regions shouldn't use `data-prop=""`.

The component controls treat an empty `data-prop` as missing, so the component gets no edit button. Primitive regions can use `data-prop=""`; components need a real key.

**Mirrors:**

- docs: visual-editing-reference.md § Empty `data-prop` pass-through

Fixtures: [src/rules/component-empty-prop](src/rules/component-empty-prop)

**Severity:** error · **Phase:** structure · **Applies to:** `source`

## source-duplicate-key

**Severity:** error · **Phase:** structure · **Applies to:** the whole page

Each `data-key` must appear once per source file.

The runtime locates a source region by searching the file for its `data-key`. If the key appears more than once, it can't tell which region to edit and shows an error card. This rule catches duplicates visible on one page; the runtime checks the raw file.

**Mirrors:**

- editable-regions/nodes/editable-source.ts:103-145

Fixtures: [src/rules/source-duplicate-key](src/rules/source-duplicate-key)

## value-region-has-children

**Severity:** warn · **Phase:** structure · **Applies to:** `text`, `image`, `source`

Text, image and source regions shouldn't contain other regions.

Value regions own their contents: text and source regions replace their inner HTML with an editor, so any regions inside them are lost as soon as editing starts.

**Mirrors:**

- editable-regions/README.md:509

Fixtures: [src/rules/value-region-has-children](src/rules/value-region-has-children)

## block-in-phrasing-host

**Severity:** warn · **Phase:** structure · **Applies to:** `text`, `source`

`data-type="block"` regions should be on an element that can hold block content.

Block text can contain lists, headings and multiple paragraphs. A `<p>` can't hold those, so the browser closes it early and the content spills out of the region. Other inline elements don't break the parse but produce invalid HTML.

**Mirrors:**

- docs: troubleshooting.md § Block content breaks the DOM around a region

Fixtures: [src/rules/block-in-phrasing-host](src/rules/block-in-phrasing-host)

## prop-attr-hyphenated

**Severity:** warn · **Phase:** structure · **Applies to:** every region

`data-prop-*` and `data-literal-*` names shouldn't contain hyphens.

The runtime reads the name through `dataset` and lowercases it, so `data-prop-author-name` becomes the key `authorname`, not `author-name` or `authorName`. HTML also lowercases attribute names, so camelCase in the attribute doesn't survive either.

**Mirrors:**

- editable-regions/nodes/editable.ts:193-217,514-515

Fixtures: [src/rules/prop-attr-hyphenated](src/rules/prop-attr-hyphenated)

## unsupported-named-prop

**Severity:** error · **Phase:** structure · **Applies to:** `image`, `text`, `source`, `array`

Text, source and array regions don't accept `data-prop-*` or `data-literal-*` attributes, and image regions only accept `src`, `alt` and `title`.

Every `data-prop-*` and `data-literal-*` attribute adds a key to the region's value, turning it into an object. Text and source regions expect a string and array regions expect an array, so they show an error card (for source regions, one that wrongly says the file doesn't exist). Image regions show an error card for any key other than `src`, `alt` or `title`.

**Mirrors:**

- editable-regions/nodes/editable.ts:255-297,503-517
- editable-regions/nodes/editable-image.ts:103-123
- editable-regions/nodes/editable-text.ts:51-73
- editable-regions/nodes/editable-source.ts:88-103
- editable-regions/nodes/editable-array.ts:121-146

Fixtures: [src/rules/unsupported-named-prop](src/rules/unsupported-named-prop)

## prop-path-malformed

**Severity:** error · **Phase:** paths · **Applies to:** every region

`data-prop` paths must be dot-separated keys, and `@collections`, `@data` and `@file` need a `[key]` in matching brackets.

The runtime splits paths on `.`, so an empty segment (`a..b`, `a.`) looks up the key `""`, which is never there. A malformed `@collections[…]`, `@data[…]` or `@file[…]` reference isn't recognised at all and is read as an unknown special prop. Either way the value is `undefined` and the region silently never becomes editable.

**Mirrors:**

- editable-regions/nodes/editable.ts:106-173,684-763

Fixtures: [src/rules/prop-path-malformed](src/rules/prop-path-malformed)

## special-prop-out-of-scope

**Severity:** error · **Phase:** paths · **Applies to:** every region

`@index` must be inside an array item and `@length` inside an array. No other `@` names exist.

Special props are passed down from the array or array item that provides them. Anywhere else, and for any other `@` name, the value is `undefined`, so the region silently never becomes editable.

**Mirrors:**

- editable-regions/nodes/editable.ts:239-250,524-527
- editable-regions/nodes/editable-array.ts:541-550
- editable-regions/nodes/editable-array-item.ts:497-504

Fixtures: [src/rules/special-prop-out-of-scope](src/rules/special-prop-out-of-scope)

## prop-unbound

**Severity:** error · **Phase:** paths · **Applies to:** every region

A relative `data-prop` must be able to reach a value through its parent region's `data-prop` or `data-prop-*` attributes.

A region looks its path up in its parent region's value, which is built from the parent's `data-prop` plus one key per `data-prop-*`. If the parent has no `data-prop` and no matching `data-prop-*`, or no props at all, the value is always `undefined`, so the region silently never becomes editable.

**Mirrors:**

- editable-regions/nodes/editable.ts:106-173,239-310,505-565
- editable-regions/nodes/editable-array.ts:42-100

Fixtures: [src/rules/prop-unbound](src/rules/prop-unbound)

## prop-target-not-found

**Severity:** error · **Phase:** data · **Applies to:** every region

`@collections[…]`, `@data[…]` and `@file[…]` must name a collection, dataset or file that exists.

The runtime looks the reference up with `CloudCannon.collection`, `CloudCannon.dataset` or `CloudCannon.file`. If there's nothing by that name, the region gets no value and silently never becomes editable.

**Mirrors:**

- editable-regions/nodes/editable.ts:529-557,707-763
- cloudcannon.config: collections_config, data_config

Fixtures: [src/rules/prop-target-not-found](src/rules/prop-target-not-found)

## prop-path-missing

**Severity:** error · **Phase:** data · **Applies to:** the whole page

Every `data-prop` path must exist in the data it points at: the page's source file, or the collection, dataset or file it references.

When a path isn't in the data, the runtime resolves it to `undefined` and the region never mounts. There's no error card: the region just isn't editable. Array items are checked by position, so an item rendered past the end of its array is reported too. For `@collections[…]`, CloudCannon's item order isn't known, so every file in the collection is checked.

**Mirrors:**

- editable-regions/nodes/editable.ts:106-173,188-194
- editable-regions/nodes/editable-array.ts:62-99

Fixtures: [src/rules/prop-path-missing](src/rules/prop-path-missing)

## prop-value-type

**Severity:** error · **Phase:** data · **Applies to:** `text`, `array`, `image`

The value a `data-prop` points at must be the type its region expects: a string for text, an array for arrays, and an object of strings for images.

Each region validates its value before rendering. Text regions need a string, arrays need an array (or a collection, dataset or file), and images need an object whose `src`, `alt` and `title` are strings. Any other type shows an error card in place of the region. `null` is always accepted.

**Mirrors:**

- editable-regions/nodes/editable-text.ts:51-75
- editable-regions/nodes/editable-array.ts:121-151
- editable-regions/nodes/editable-image.ts:61-100

Fixtures: [src/rules/prop-value-type](src/rules/prop-value-type)
